title: Introduce health-proxy and backpressure policies to stabilize autoscaling during multi-region failovers
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: During last quarter's multi-region incident we observed rapid autoscaler oscillation and large-scale load shedding when a subset of hosts in a region transitioned between noisy-success and transient-failure states. The immediate cause was tightly coupled readiness/liveness signals that fed directly into scaling decisions and global routing. That coupling allowed short-lived backend degradation to cause autoscalers to scale down capacity, which then created cascading failures and SLO breaches (p95 latency spikes and error-budget burn).

Problem statement: We need to decouple raw process-level health signals from autoscaler admission decisions and global routing to avoid throttle-then-crash cycles during partial-region degradations. Current probes are binary and have no temporal smoothing or priority weighting across request classes. Autoscaler reacts to these binary signals too aggressively, causing capacity churn and increased tail latency.

Goals:
- Prevent autoscaler thrashing and unnecessary capacity evictions during transient probe noise.
- Ensure failover and traffic shifting preserve SLOs (p95 latency and availability) for high-priority customers.
- Provide observability and controls so SREs can tune aggressive vs. conservative modes per deployment and per region.

Proposed solution (summary): Implement a lightweight in-cluster "health-proxy" that mediates liveness/readiness readings and emits a graded health score to downstream consumers (autoscaler, router, circuit breakers). Complement the proxy with a backpressure policy layer that applies a token-bucket style admission control and time-windowed derating before the autoscaler is allowed to scale down capacity for a host/pool. Key components:
1) Health proxy: consolidates probe results (liveness, readiness, synthetic transactions) and external telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates) into a 0-100 health-score. Exposes a small gRPC/HTTP endpoint used by autoscaler and load balancer for decisioning. Health calculation parameters are configurable via ConfigMap/Console.
2) Soft-state readiness: hosts report graded readiness (green/yellow/red) not binary ready/not-ready. Yellow indicates degraded but serving with constrained concurrency. Router will apply traffic shedding and per-route throttles to yellow hosts rather than immediate ejection.
3) Backpressure policy: before autoscaler triggers scale-down, the backpressure layer imposes graduated derating windows (e.g., 2m soft, 10m cooldown) and enforces a minimum healthy-host fraction per region. A token-bucket is used for short bursts of ejections to prevent mass scale-down.
4) Circuit breaker integration: the health-score feeds the existing circuit-breaker matrix to choose fallback model variants/regions, with explicit weighting to prefer warm regions and Dedicated capacity.

Tradeoffs:
- Adds another control surface (health-proxy) that must be shipped and maintained; however it centralizes complex heuristics and avoids widespread changes to existing autoscaler code.
- Graded readiness delays immediate isolation of truly unhealthy hosts; mitigation: include synthetic transaction thresholds and absolute error thresholds that still force immediate ejection if crossed.

Metrics and SLO mapping:
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for hosted API; availability >= 99.9% for production tenants.
- New metrics to track: health_score_distribution, time_in_yellow_per_host, backpressure_token_levels, autoscaler_scale_events_by_cause.
- Alerting: when health_score volatility increases > 3x baseline or when the backpressure token bucket drains to < 20% for > 5m.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: unit/integration tests + sim harness (dev cluster) to validate scoring and token-bucket behavior against synthetic failure modes.
- Phase 1 (canary): Enable health-proxy read-only in staging and feed autoscaler a passive score (no control). Monitor discrepancies for 48h.
- Phase 2 (controlled canary): Enable graded readiness plus conservative backpressure in a single low-traffic region (eus-1) for 7 days. Start at 1% traffic, progress to 10% if stable.
- Phase 3 (broader): Gradual ramp to all hosted regions behind a feature flag with per-environment tuning via Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Under a simulated 10% host failure in a region, autoscaler does not scale down more than 2x baseline hosts within 15 minutes.
- p95 latency remains within 1.2x baseline during graceful degradation tests.
- No customer-facing errors introduced by proxy in canary runs; any regressions cause immediate rollback flag.

Follow-ups: fine-grained Console UI for health thresholds, per-customer minimal capacity reservation, and an SLO-aware autoscaler mode that consumes health_score and projected error-budget burn rate.

2026-02-12 - Diego Rivera: added token-bucket backpressure design and canary rollout sequence; flagged dependency on autoscaler PR for read-score endpoint.
2026-02-15 - SRE review (Liam Ortiz): suggested emergency-eject thresholds for absolute failure modes; requested synthetic transaction integration.
2026-02-18 - PM feedback (Priya Nair): prioritize regions with highest SLA customers first; requested explicit communication plan for enterprise customers on Dedicated capacity behavior.
2026-02-22 - Engineering note (Diego Rivera): implemented sim harness that can replay request-shape distributions; preliminary runs show 35% reduction in scale churn for noisy-90s failures.

acceptance_criteria: Canary run for 7 days with no increase in customer-visible errors and controlled scale activity as defined in the rollout plan
Simulated partial-region failures show autoscaler scale-down limited per spec and p95 latency within target
Metrics for health_score, backpressure_token_levels, and autoscaler_scale_events are visible in Console and have baseline alert thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for health-score computation covering edge cases (synthetic failure, transient errors, high tail latency)
Integration tests: autoscaler reads health_score and respects backpressure cooldown windows in a local k8s environment
Chaos tests in sim-harness: replay past incident traffic and measure scale event deltas and latency impact
Canary validation checklist: stable metrics for 48h, step-up to 10% only if no alerts
